newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates ease after import demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates ease after import demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates eased after textile mill owners demanded duty-free imports of one million 375-lb bales to compensate for an expected shortfall in the cotton crop, estimated by textile magnates at 9.0 million bales, compared to a targeted 10 million, dealers said.
Rates, which jumped on the lower estimates, fell when growers released stocks they had been holding, said broker Khushi Ram at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA).
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 fell to 2,100 rupees ($52.52) per maund (37.32 kg) and was likely to open lower on Thursday, the broker said.
